message.content:
<root_cause>
  <trajectory_summary>
  In turns 46–60 the agent focused on locating downloadable macro datasets (IMF WEO and PWT) via command-line probing and then inspecting the provided Excel template structure. Turn 46 successfully discovered working IMF WEO bulk download URLs for some vintages (e.g., WEOApr2024all.xls, WEOOct2024all.xls, WEOApr2025all.xls), but no WEO data were subsequently extracted or written into test-supply.xlsx. Turns 47–49 inspected the workbook and found it contains zero formulas across all sheets and largely empty input areas. Turns 51–60 downloaded PWT 11.0 (Excel) from Dataverse and successfully extracted Georgia’s PWT variables (rnna, rkna) and their definitions from the Legend sheet, after resolving an initial mistake of reading the wrong sheet and after interrupting a long-running parse attempt. No Playwright-based browsing was used in this window, and no Excel edits/saves were made; therefore the required data population, HP filter via Solver, production function extension, and shock simulation were not completed in the output file.
  </trajectory_summary>
  <what_worked>
    <item>Turn 46: Identified valid IMF WEO bulk download endpoints (HTTP 200) for multiple releases, e.g., “200 https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Publications/WEO/WEO-Database/2024/April/WEOApr2024all.xls” and “200 .../2025/April/WEOApr2025all.xls”.</item>
    <item>Turn 51: Successfully downloaded the PWT 11.0 Excel file from Dataverse (“curl -L -o /root/data/pwt11.xlsx 'https://dataverse.nl/api/access/datafile/554105'” produced a 5.6MB file).</item>
    <item>Turn 58: Successfully parsed Georgia (GEO) time series values for rnna and rkna from the PWT “Data” sheet (“rows 74 ... last3 [(2021, 409189.75, 1), (2022, 415085.84375, 1.017875...), (2023, 426190.5, 1.054265...)]”).</item>
    <item>Turn 59–60: Correctly retrieved PWT metadata/definitions from the Legend sheet, confirming variable meanings (e.g., “rnna Capital stock at constant 2021 national prices (in mil. 2021US$)” and “delta Average depreciation rate of the capital stock”).</item>
  </what_worked>
  <issues>
    <issue>
      <where>turns 47–49</where>
      <evidence>The agent found “Production formulas 0 ... WEO_Data formulas 0” (turn 48) and that most rows were empty (turn 49 shows rows 28–34 all None, with only headers like “K/Y”, “K”, “Y”, etc. in row 35).</evidence>
      <cause>No required workbook population occurred; the agent only inspected the template instead of entering/linking data and formulas needed for the HP filter, projections, and production function steps.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turns 46–60</where>
      <evidence>The task requires “ONLY use excel” and “Use Playwright MCP” for IMF WEO; however actions used terminal curl/python/openpyxl and there are no Playwright tool calls or Excel/Solver operations shown in this window.</evidence>
      <cause>The agent followed a command-line data acquisition/debugging approach rather than executing the specified Excel-only workflow (including Solver-based HP filter) and Playwright-based WEO extraction.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turn 52</where>
      <evidence>The agent attempted to read headers from the first sheet of PWT (“Info”) and failed: “ValueError: 'countrycode' is not in list”.</evidence>
      <cause>Incorrect sheet selection/assumption about where the main dataset resides (the dataset is in the “Data” sheet, not the first sheet).</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turns 53–57</where>
      <evidence>Parsing the PWT Data sheet with cell-based access stalled (“Process still running (soft timeout)”), requiring an interrupt (turn 57 shows KeyboardInterrupt inside openpyxl read-only parsing).</evidence>
      <cause>Inefficient access pattern (random-access ws.cell calls over a very large read-only sheet) caused slow streaming XML parsing; needed iter_rows(values_only=True) to be performant (which was used successfully in turn 58).</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turn 50</where>
      <evidence>The agent summed an 8-year investment schedule to 10583.8 (units unclear), which contradicts the stated total “6.5 billion USD” investment lasting 8 years.</evidence>
      <cause>Investment path values appear inconsistent with the task’s total-shock constraint and/or with workbook unit conventions (USD vs millions), but no reconciliation or Excel-based implementation followed.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turns 46–60</where>
      <evidence>Although WEO .xls URLs were discovered (turn 46), no subsequent download/parsing of the WEO file and no population of the “WEO_Data” sheet occurred (earlier summary notes WEO_Data numeric rows count = 0 and nothing in this window contradicts that).</evidence>
      <cause>The agent stopped at URL discovery and shifted to PWT exploration; the core dependency (WEO real GDP level and growth for 2000–2027 and extension to 2043) remained unfulfilled.</cause>
    </issue>
  </issues>
  <outcome_assessment value="likely_failure">The run did not populate test-supply.xlsx with the required WEO/ECB/PWT data, formulas, Solver-based HP filter, or production-function computations; it only located/downloaded PWT and identified WEO file URLs without executing the Excel-only modeling steps.</outcome_assessment>
</root_cause>
message.reasoning:
**Analyzing root causes**

I need to produce a root cause analysis in XML. First, I see I didn't use Excel or Playwright; instead, I opted for Python to inspect, but I didn't populate the workbook or include formulas. I'm still blocked on the WEO and ECB. On a positive note, PWT parsing succeeded, which is good. However, there’s an issue with the long-running openpyxl in read-only mode causing a timeout. Also, there's a mismatch in investment schedules that suggests errors in earlier computations. The outcome is likely a failure since Excel wasn't filled, and the model wasn't run. On the upside, I found URLs for the IMF WEO for 2024/2025 and successfully downloaded the PWT file.
